members.name: PromptEncoderConfig
members.signature: PromptEncoderConfig(task_type: TaskType | str | None = None, peft_type: PeftType | str | None = None, auto_mapping: dict[str, str] | None = None, base_model_name_or_path: str | None = None, revision: str | None = None, inference_mode: bool = False, num_virtual_tokens: int | None = None, token_dim: int | None = None, num_transformer_submodules: int | None = None, num_attention_heads: int | None = None, num_layers: int | None = None, modules_to_save: list[str] | None = None, encoder_reparameterization_type: PromptEncoderReparameterizationType | str = PromptEncoderReparameterizationType.MLP, encoder_hidden_size: int | None = None, encoder_num_layers: int = 2, encoder_dropout: float = 0.0)
members.summary: How `lucid.peft.get_peft_model` adapts a model with p-tuning.
members.extended:
P-tuning (Liu et al., 2021, [arXiv:2103.10385](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.10385)) puts `num_virtual_tokens`
learned embeddings in front of the input like prompt tuning, but produces
them through an encoder — an MLP, or a bidirectional LSTM followed by one —
so the tokens depend on each other.  The encoder is only used while
training: the file stores the prompt it produced.

Field names, defaults and `adapter_config.json` are the reference adapter
library's.  Every field is keyword-only.

parameters.name: task_type
parameters.description: The task the adapter is for (metadata; see `TaskType`).

parameters.name: peft_type
parameters.description:
The method; filled in by the subclass when omitted, refused when
it names another.

parameters.name: auto_mapping
parameters.description:
The class of the base model, `{"base_model_class": name,
"parent_library": module}` — what `AutoPeftModel*` rebuilds the
base with.  `PeftModel.save_pretrained` writes it.

parameters.name: base_model_name_or_path
parameters.description: Name of the model the adapter was trained on (metadata).

parameters.name: inference_mode
parameters.description: Freeze the adapter too, for inference.

parameters.name: num_virtual_tokens
parameters.description: How many learned embeddings go in front of the input.

parameters.name: num_transformer_submodules
parameters.description:
`1` for an encoder-only or decoder-only model, `2` for an
encoder-decoder one; `2` for `task_type="SEQ_2_SEQ_LM"` and `1`
otherwise when omitted.

parameters.name: modules_to_save
parameters.description:
Modules of the model trained in full beside the prompt (a
classification head).

parameters.name: encoder_num_layers
parameters.description: LSTM layers (an MLP always has two hidden layers; a different value warns).

raises.description: A field holds a value of the wrong type.

examples:
>>> from lucid.peft import PromptEncoderConfig
>>> config = PromptEncoderConfig(num_virtual_tokens=4, encoder_reparameterization_type="LSTM")
>>> config.peft_type, config.encoder_reparameterization_type
(<PeftType.P_TUNING: 'P_TUNING'>, <PromptEncoderReparameterizationType.LSTM: 'LSTM'>)

members.name: PromptEncoderReparameterizationType
members.summary: What turns the virtual tokens' embeddings into the prompt: an `MLP` or an `LSTM`.

members.name: PromptEncoder

methods.name: __init__
methods.summary: Build the virtual-token embedding and the head that maps it to the prompt.
methods.extended:
The head is the MLP, or the bidirectional LSTM and an MLP, that
`config.encoder_reparameterization_type` names; an `inference_mode` encoder has no
head.

methods.name: from_config
methods.summary: The encoder for `config`.
methods.extended: `word_embeddings` is not read, the encoder makes its own.

methods.name: stores_prompt
methods.summary: `True` when no head maps the embedding (an `inference_mode` encoder).
methods.extended: Its rows are then the finished prompt.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Prompt rows of the virtual-token ids: `(B, total)` ids to `(B, total, token_dim)`.

methods.name: per_task
methods.summary: Whether the prompt depends on the task each batch row belongs to (`task_ids`).

methods.name: stored
methods.summary: The tensors an adapter file holds, by the encoder's own key and the file's: the prompt always, and whatever else the method keeps beside it.

methods.name: num_embeddings
methods.summary: How many virtual tokens the encoder produces.

methods.name: indices
methods.summary: The virtual-token ids `(1, num_embeddings)` the encoder is called with.

methods.name: prompts
methods.summary: The prompt of each of `batch` rows: `(batch, num_embeddings, width)`.
methods.extended:
`tasks` is the task of each row, which a `per_task` encoder needs and the others
do not read.

methods.name: prompt_embeddings
methods.summary: The prompt as an adapter file stores it: `(rows, width)`, one row per virtual token.

members.summary: The prompt of p-tuning: virtual-token embeddings through an MLP, or a bidirectional LSTM and an MLP.
members.extended:
Built for a trainable adapter it holds the whole encoder; built with
`inference_mode` it holds `embedding` alone, whose rows are then the
prompt (as an adapter file stores it).

parameters.name: config
parameters.description:
Sizes (`num_virtual_tokens`, `num_transformer_submodules`,
`token_dim`, `encoder_hidden_size` set) and the encoder's type.

examples:
>>> import lucid
>>> from lucid.peft import PromptEncoderConfig
>>> from lucid.peft.tuners.p_tuning import PromptEncoder
>>> config = PromptEncoderConfig(num_virtual_tokens=3, token_dim=8, encoder_hidden_size=16,
...                              num_transformer_submodules=1)
>>> PromptEncoder(config)(lucid.arange(3).long().reshape(1, 3)).shape
(1, 3, 8)

methods.name: active_adapters
methods.summary: The adapter the model is prompted with, as a list.
methods.extended: Prompt learning applies one at a time.

methods.name: add_adapter
methods.signature: add_adapter(adapter_name: str, peft_config: PeftConfig, low_cpu_mem_usage: bool = False)
methods.summary: Add a prompt beside the ones held; it starts frozen, and `set_adapter` switches to it.

raises.description: The name is taken, or the config is another method's.

methods.name: set_adapter
methods.signature: set_adapter(adapter_name: str | list[str], inference_mode: bool = False)
methods.summary: Apply the named prompt — one at a time — and train it unless `inference_mode`.

methods.name: set_requires_grad
methods.signature: set_requires_grad(adapter_names: str | Sequence[str], requires_grad: bool = True)
methods.summary: Set `requires_grad` on the named adapters' encoders and `modules_to_save` copies.

methods.name: delete_adapter
methods.summary: Remove a prompt and its `modules_to_save` copies; another takes over if it was in use.

methods.name: unload
methods.summary: Take the hooks and the `modules_to_save` copies out and give every parameter its old `requires_grad`.

methods.name: merge_and_unload
methods.signature: merge_and_unload(progressbar: bool = False, safe_merge: bool = False, adapter_names: list[str] | None = None)
methods.summary: Refused: a prompt has no weight to fold into the model.

methods.name: enable_adapter_layers
methods.summary: Prompt the model again, and run the trained `modules_to_save` copies.

methods.name: disable_adapter_layers
methods.summary: Stop prompting.
methods.extended: The model runs as the base does, and its `modules_to_save` modules run their originals.

methods.name: forward
methods.summary: Call the model.
methods.extended: The prompt is put in by hooks on the model's own call, so nothing is applied here.

members.summary: The tuner of p-tuning: a `PromptEncoder` per adapter, whose prompt goes in front of the input.

summary: `lucid.peft.tuners.p_tuning` — p-tuning: virtual tokens produced by an MLP or LSTM.
extended:
P-tuning (Liu et al., 2021, [arXiv:2103.10385](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.10385) — "GPT Understands, Too") puts `num_virtual_tokens`
learned embeddings in front of the input like prompt tuning, but produces them through an encoder,
an MLP or a bidirectional LSTM followed by one, so the tokens depend on each other.  The encoder is
only used while training: the file stores the prompt it produced.  Pick it over prompt tuning when
independent token embeddings train poorly.

The prompt is applied by hooks on the model's own call.  Here: `PromptEncoder` (what is learned)
and `PromptEncoderModel` (the tuner).  `PromptEncoderConfig` and
`PromptEncoderReparameterizationType` are here too and exported from `lucid.peft`.
citation: Liu, Xiao, et al. "GPT Understands, Too." [arXiv:2103.10385](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.10385), 2021.
theory:
P-tuning (Liu et al., 2021, [arXiv:2103.10385](https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.10385)) puts `num_virtual_tokens`
learned embeddings in front of the input like prompt tuning, but produces
them through an encoder — an MLP, or a bidirectional LSTM followed by one —
so the tokens depend on each other.  The encoder is only used while
training: the file stores the prompt it produced.
